causal_assumptions.consistency: Training groups receive the study-specific number of instrumental sessions.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Supported by randomized assignment within each experiment or laboratory.

claims.causal_estimand: Difference between extended and moderate training in the valued-versus-devalued response contrast.

confidence.rationale: One influential experiment reported the predicted interaction, while a larger preregistered four-laboratory study found no statistical effect of training duration.

limitations: Food satiation may incompletely or nonspecifically alter outcome value.

boundary_conditions: Selective satiation must actually alter outcome value for each participant.
Null training effects do not establish absence of every form of habit learning.
scope.population: Healthy adults completing free-operant food outcome-devaluation tasks.
scope.temporal_scope: One versus multiple training sessions followed by devaluation and extinction testing.

claims.statement: Extended instrumental training has not shown a robust general causal effect on outcome-insensitive responding in humans.
claims.temporal_ordering: Training assignment precedes outcome devaluation and the extinction test.

causal_assumptions.consistency: Assigned stress and control conditions follow the original protocols closely.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Both stress and control conditions are represented.

claims.causal_estimand: Stress-versus-control difference in responding for devalued relative to valued outcomes.

confidence.rationale: Both experiments successfully induced stress but failed to support the predicted stress-by-devaluation effect; interpretation was limited by poor goal-directed differentiation in controls.

limitations: Indifferent control-group responding made the intended mechanistic contrast difficult to interpret.

boundary_conditions: The result does not exclude stress effects under other tasks, stressors, or timing arrangements.
scope.population: Healthy adults in food-reward instrumental-learning tasks.
scope.temporal_scope: Stress before or immediately after learning, followed by satiation and extinction testing.

claims.statement: Acute stress did not reliably increase outcome-insensitive responding in two preregistered exact human replications.
claims.temporal_ordering: Stress assignment occurs before the post-devaluation test.

confidence.rationale: A large Registered Report tested six paradigms and found no overlap across experimental approaches or with real-life habit self-report.

claims.confounding_note: Cross-sectional score associations can be attenuated by measurement error, restricted variance, and task-specific processes.

estimate.metric: preregistered cross-task correlations and measurement-model fit
estimate.notes: The study reported no evidence for overlap across experimental habit measures or self-reported real-life habits.

boundary_conditions: A young convenience sample and task reliability can constrain correlations.
scope.population: 208 healthy young adults contributing to cross-task analyses.
scope.temporal_scope: Five-day laboratory assessment plus online measures.

claims.statement: Scores from different laboratory and self-report habit paradigms did not show evidence of a common convergent habit measure.

confidence.rationale: Outcome-insensitive behavior is theoretically diagnostic only after effective devaluation and comprehension checks, while human induction and measurement results remain inconsistent.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The operational account is challenged when purported habit effects disappear after individual verification of devaluation, task knowledge, baseline responding, and response opportunity.
limitations: Current evidence does not identify a unitary human habit mechanism across paradigms.

boundary_conditions: Does not equate habits with repetition, speed, automaticity, model-free choice, or procedural skill.
scope.temporal_scope: Instrumental training followed by a diagnostic test without corrective feedback.

claims.statement: A cue-linked control process can contribute to instrumental responding without immediate use of current outcome value.
claims.temporal_ordering: Instrumental learning and verified devaluation precede the outcome-sensitivity test.

evidence.design: One-day versus three-day free-operant food training followed by selective satiation and an extinction test.

effect.notes: F(1,29)=7.9, p<.05; the three-day group persisted more for the devalued food outcome.

limitations: Small sample and incomplete separation of devaluation effectiveness from habitual control.
Neural correlates do not establish the causal mechanism.
evidence.population: Healthy adults; behavioral interaction reported with 31 analyzed participants.
evidence.summary: Extended training was associated with reduced behavioral sensitivity to selective satiation in the original experiment.

evidence.design: Preregistered four-laboratory moderate-versus-extended training study adapting the Tricomi free-operant task.

effect.metric: preregistered main effect of training amount on habit expression
effect.notes: No statistical evidence was found for a main effect of training amount; stress moderation was exploratory.

limitations: Selective satiation and baseline outcome sensitivity remained important interpretive constraints.
evidence.population: Healthy adult participants recruited across four laboratories.
evidence.summary: The multilaboratory study did not reproduce a general increase in outcome-insensitive responding after extended training.

evidence.design: Preregistered exact replication with acute stress before instrumental learning and a post-satiation extinction test.

effect.metric: stress by outcome-value interaction on high-probability choices
effect.notes: Stress induction succeeded, but Bayesian analyses supported the null habit-shift hypothesis.

evidence.extraction_locator: Study 1 Methods and Results; General Discussion.
limitations: Control participants did not clearly differentiate valued from devalued outcomes at test.
evidence.population: Healthy adults assigned to stress or no-stress control.
evidence.summary: Stress before learning did not increase devalued responding relative to control.

evidence.design: Preregistered exact replication with acute stress immediately after instrumental learning and a post-satiation extinction test.

effect.metric: stress by outcome-value interaction on high-probability choices
effect.notes: The second experiment also failed to support stress-induced habitual responding.

evidence.extraction_locator: Study 2 Methods and Results; General Discussion.
limitations: Indiscriminate devaluation weakened the intended diagnostic comparison.
evidence.population: Healthy adults assigned to stress or no-stress control.
evidence.summary: Stress after learning did not produce the predicted shift toward devalued responding.

evidence.design: Five-day Registered Report with six experimental habit paradigms, computational analyses, and real-life habit self-report.

effect.notes: No evidence for overlap among experimental habit approaches or with self-reported real-life habits.

evidence.extraction_locator: Registered Report abstract; Participants; validity of habit tasks; RQ3-RQ5.
limitations: Young convenience sample and reliability differences can attenuate cross-task associations.
evidence.population: 220 healthy adults in the full sample; 208 in cross-task analyses.
evidence.summary: Different operationalizations did not behave as interchangeable measures of one common habit construct.

metadata.description: Human experiments separating instrumental behavior, outcome value, devaluation sensitivity, training duration, acute stress, measurement, and proposed habitual or goal-directed control mechanisms.
metadata.title: Primary evidence pack for habitual and goal-directed action control

objects.definition: Laboratory task in which actions first produce valued outcomes and responding is later tested after one outcome loses value.
objects.label: Instrumental outcome-devaluation task
objects.scope: Human food or monetary outcome-devaluation paradigms.

objects.definition: Study context administering several laboratory habit tasks and self-report measures to test convergence across operationalizations.
objects.label: Multi-paradigm habit assessment
objects.scope: Nebe et al. 2024 Registered Report in healthy young adults.

boundary_notes: Programmed devaluation does not guarantee that subjective value changed for every participant.
Value of one outcome must remain distinguishable from generalized satiety or disengagement.
objects.definition: Time-indexed motivational value of a particular action outcome for a person.
objects.label: Current outcome value

objects.definition: Observable action performed in a specified action-outcome contingency.
objects.function_note: Repetition or speed alone does not establish habitual control.
objects.label: Instrumental response
objects.response_topography: Task-specific button press, key choice, or response withholding.

objects.definition: Continued instrumental responding after a demonstrated reduction in the value of its specific outcome, relative to an appropriate valued-outcome comparison.
objects.function_note: This pattern is compatible with habit but can also arise from failed devaluation, misunderstanding, low baseline responding, or measurement error.
objects.label: Outcome-insensitive response pattern

objects.definition: Experimental assignment to substantially more repetitions or sessions of an action-outcome contingency.
objects.delivery: Multiple instrumental-training sessions compared with a shorter-training condition.
objects.label: Extended instrumental training

objects.definition: Experimental manipulation intended to reduce the current value of one trained action outcome while preserving the value of another.
objects.delivery: Outcome-specific satiation, taste aversion, instruction, or conversion of reward to loss.
objects.label: Selective outcome devaluation

objects.definition: Controlled experimental procedure designed to increase acute subjective and physiological stress before or after instrumental learning.
objects.delivery: Cold pressor or comparable stress protocol with a nonstress control condition.
objects.label: Acute stress induction

objects.definition: Proposed action-selection process that uses action-outcome knowledge and current outcome value to guide responding.
objects.label: Goal-directed action control
realization_conditions: The actor has usable knowledge of the action-outcome relation.
Current outcome value can influence action selection before responding.

boundary_notes: Automaticity, repetition, procedural skill, and model-free choice are not exact synonyms.
Outcome insensitivity supports habitual control only when devaluation and task comprehension are verified.
objects.definition: Proposed cue-linked action-selection process whose momentary expression is relatively insensitive to the current value of the action outcome.
objects.label: Habitual action control
realization_conditions: A learned cue-response relation is available in the test context.
Outcome value has changed effectively and is not required for immediate response selection.

objects.definition: Contrast in responding for still-valued versus effectively devalued trained outcomes.
objects.label: Outcome-devaluation sensitivity index
objects.method: Compare response rates or choices after outcome-specific devaluation, ideally with individual manipulation checks.

objects.definition: Correlation or latent convergence among scores from distinct laboratory and self-report habit measures.
objects.label: Cross-task habit-measure convergence
objects.method: Estimate preregistered correlations and measurement models across multiple habit operationalizations.

boundary_notes: Lack of convergence can reflect different mechanisms, low reliability, or restricted variance.
objects.definition: Degree to which distinct habit measures behave as indicators of a shared latent attribute or process.
objects.label: Habit-measurement convergence

sources.authority_note: Influential primary experiment reporting training-dependent human outcome insensitivity.
sources.title: A specific role for posterior dorsolateral striatum in human habit learning

sources.authority_note: Preregistered four-laboratory investigation of the critical training-duration effect.
sources.title: Determining the effects of training duration on the behavioral expression of habitual control in humans: a multilaboratory investigation

sources.authority_note: Two preregistered exact replications preserving null stress effects and manipulation failures.
sources.title: Does stress consistently favor habits over goal-directed behaviors? Data from two preregistered exact replication studies

sources.authority_note: Large Registered Report directly testing convergence across six laboratory habit paradigms and self-report.
sources.title: Characterizing Human Habits in the Lab
